source.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Matteo Boglioni; Thibault Rousset; Siva Reddy; Marius Mosbach; Verna Dankers

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests fine-tuning resurfacing of unlearned PII and whether unlearning changes the known storage weights, using a synthetic masked-injection testbed and localization metrics.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own resurfacing attack and localization-precision results. The paper also reports forget/retain and general-utility metrics, but these are not itemized here because the reported result set would exceed the 60-row limit. The Jaccard similarities describe overlap between leaked profiles, not recovery rates. Cited resurfacing and relearning results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own resurfacing attack fine-tunes unlearned OLMo2 1B and OLMo3 7B models on held-out PII and counts leaked forget-set profiles (B; F for OracleGrad). Ground-truth localization AUC tests whether methods edit the storage weights (C, analysis part). Output-level forget, utility and paraphrase tables bear on A and E. It uses a different method from the originals on the same erase-vs-obfuscate question.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the authors say SimNPO and OracleGrad are equally resistant on numerical fields. They also say lower 7B resurfacing may reflect a limitation of their straightforward attack rather than the model.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates SimNPO, AlphaEdit, MemFlex, and an introduced oracle method on synthetic PII injected into known parameter masks; resurfacing uses instruction-tuning on separate held-out PII data. It is not a reproduction of the original source methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Resurfacing rates vary by model size, PII field, and unlearning method. The paper notes OLMo3 7B is generally less prone to resurfacing, with an isolated exception for MemFlex on phone numbers.

fits_no_version.finding: Leaked-profile Jaccard overlap: SimNPO and OracleGrad leak largely the same profiles (Jaccard 1.00 on driver's license).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual recoverable knowledge after unlearning concentrates on specific hard-to-unlearn data points shared across methods.

record.code_released: not stated (repository name in text: McGill-NLP/LACUNA)
record.problems: Synthetic injected PII and a particular instruction-tuning resurfacing attack limit generalization to other knowledge and attacks. The attack is described as straightforward; the authors caution that lower leakage on 7B may reflect attack limitations. Resurfacing figures provide rates without reported uncertainty. The retained rows do not include the full output-level and utility metric tables.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within 60 rows, omitted the four OLMo3 7B email-address localization AUC results reported in Table 3; the 28 other method/model/field AUC rows and all 32 resurfacing-rate rows are retained. The main text also reports output-level forget/retain and utility measures in Figures 4, 7, 9 and Tables 2–3; these were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts, or on fully unrelated data; only held-out PII of other synthetic people is used.
Activation-direction ablation is not tested. Only weight-level localization analysis is reported.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information; only template paraphrases, used as an evaluation metric rather than an attack.
OracleGrad is not tested against ablation, quantization or prompting attacks. No deployable counter-method is tested.

missing.what: Output-level forget EM/ES/Prob, retain and utility deltas per method/model/field. Declared as not extracted, but needed for the A verdict (near-chance forgetting and utility cost).
Paraphrased-prompt forget metrics showing no recovery by rephrasing.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1–V6 ids were mapped to A–F. Several resurfacing values were reassigned, using the Jaccard-matrix diagonals (an empty leaked set gives 0.00) and footnote 12; bar readouts remain uncertain for birth city. The study reports no pre-attack Success@200 baseline, so leakage without fine-tuning is unknown. The attack is LoRA instruction tuning on the last two layers, which lie outside the masked storage weights. AlphaEdit's AUC of exactly 0.500 partly reflects that it only edits layers 4–8.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports output-level forget and utility evaluations, but the rows retained here do not record those metrics separately; the resurfacing rows test the attack-resistance part of this version, not whether initial targeted accuracy is near chance.
Tests instruction-tuning on a separate held-out PII dataset, not fine-tuning on unrelated or loosely related examples, a small subset of forgotten facts, or the exact examples specified in the claim.

No activation-direction ablation is tested. Localization precision is measured against a ground-truth injection mask; this is evidence about targeting storage weights, not a direct demonstration of the access-blocking mechanism.
Prompt rephrasing is evaluated as an output metric, but prompt-only attacks, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested as recovery attacks.
OracleGrad is tested against the paper’s instruction-tuning resurfacing attack only; it is not tested against ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.

relationships.display_finding: AlphaEdit retained exact-match scores of 63.2% for 1B email targets and 46.5% for 7B birth-city targets; fine-tuning recovered 74–87% of email profiles for MemFlex and AlphaEdit on 1B.
